paper_title: Public Key Encryption Secure Against Quantum Leakage
authors: Alper Cakan, Fuyuki Kitagawa, Ryo Nishimaki, Manasi Shingane, and Takashi Yamakawa

context: In the non-adaptive leakage model, where the leakage function cannot depend on the public key, we can rely on the classical leakage resilience of the one-time SKE scheme to prove classical leakage resilience of the resulting PKE scheme. On the other hand, the insecurity of the one-time SKE scheme against quantum leakage directly lifts to insecurity of the resulting PKE scheme against quantum leakage. This gives a separation in the non-adaptive leakage model. Unfortunately, this idea does not work in the adaptive leakage model considered in this work. Indeed, the above scheme is trivially insecure even against classical leakage in the adaptive leakage model: once the public key is available, the leakage function can simply recover and output the secret key of the base PKE scheme. Thus, we leave open the problem of separating classical and quantum leakage resilience in the adaptive leakage model. 1.3 Related Works Classical leakage-resilient PKE Many works have studied leakage-resilient PKE in the classical bounded-leakage model [AGV09, NS09, HLWW16, BLSV18]. In particular, prior works establish a tradeoff between assumptions and achievable leakage ratios in the classical-leakage setting [HLWW16, BLSV18]. Our work gives an analogous tradeoff in the presence of quantum leakage. Classical leakage-resilient PKE has also been studied in several other models, including the bounded-retrieval model [DLW06, Dzi06, ADW09], the auxiliary-input leakage model [DKL09], and the continual-leakage model [BKKV10, DHLW10]. Extending these models to the quantumleakage setting is beyond the scope of this paper and is left for future work. We refer to [KR19] for a more extensive survey of the classical leakage-resilience literature.
